title: Choose the homepage composition
question: All three use Systems Wayfinding. Choose one, or steer a combination by naming what should carry forward.

options.label: Route Spine
options.lineage: one diagnostic route governs the entire scroll
options.thesis: The proposition and architecture map meet at one junction that branches directly into the three service outcomes.
options.viewport: Headline and founder note occupy the light half; a detailed blue architecture field occupies the other half; the route visibly branches into services below.
options.risk: The dense architecture half needs careful semantic simplification so it feels authoritative rather than dashboard-like.

options.label: Decision Field
options.lineage: the evidence field leads and content behaves like its legend
options.thesis: A full-width architecture map is the homepage’s primary evidence, with copy, founder judgment, and actions attached to its perimeter.
options.viewport: The map dominates the fold; a white action legend overlaps the lower-left while João’s verdict attaches to the chosen path on the right.
options.risk: The evidence field has the strongest impact but requires the most disciplined mobile reduction and accessible diagram labeling.

options.label: Folded Atlas
options.lineage: one system map folded into proposition, architecture, and decision planes
options.thesis: Three unequal planes give the headline, system evidence, and primary decision distinct roles while one route binds them together.
options.viewport: A light proposition plane, a dominant blue topology plane, and a narrow decision rail create the most editorial and architectural silhouette.
options.risk: The right decision rail can become cramped in Portuguese and must transform decisively rather than merely shrink.
